beats.text: A limit describes nearby outputs, even when the input itself is missing. This quotient is undefined at one because its denominator is zero. The graph can still approach a definite height from both sides.
Factor the entire numerator as x minus one times x plus one. For nearby inputs other than one, the shared factor is nonzero, so its ratio equals one. Cancelling factors preserves these nearby values.

The simpler expression approaches two as x approaches one. Therefore the original quotient has limit two, although it has no value at one. Taking a limit and assigning a function value are different operations.

Both sides must agree for a two-sided limit. Absolute x divided by x equals negative one on the left and positive one on the right. These different destination heights prevent a two-sided limit at zero.

practice.prompt: Find the limit of 5x−4 as x approaches 2. Explain why substitution is valid here.
practice.answer: The polynomial is continuous, so the limit is 5(2)−4=6.

practice.prompt: Find lim x→−2 (x²−4)/(x+2). Show the factorization and keep the original excluded input.
practice.answer: For x≠−2, (x²−4)/(x+2)=(x−2)(x+2)/(x+2)=x−2. The limit is −4; the original is still undefined at −2.

practice.prompt: Let g(x)=3x−2 for x≠1, but g(1)=100. Find the limit at 1 and decide whether g is continuous there.
practice.answer: Nearby outputs approach 1, so the limit is 1. Since g(1)=100, g is not continuous at 1.

takeaway: Simplification on nearby allowed inputs can reveal a limit without filling a missing function value.
scope: First lesson on removable gaps, legal cancellation, and agreement of one-sided limits.
title: Limits and simplification
objective: Evaluate limits by valid algebra near a point while preserving the original domain.
